[[Reykjavík]], Iceland | capacity = 2,781 (1,541 seated) | chairman = [[Magnús Orri Schram]] | manager = [[Óskar Hrafn Þorvaldsson]] | league = [[Besta deild karla]] | season = [[2025 Besta deild karla|2025]] | position = Besta deild karla, 10th of 12 | current = 2020 Knattspyrnufélag Reykjavíkur season | website = {{official URL}} | pattern_la1 = _black_stripes_thin1 | pattern_b1 = _nikestripeddiv4wb | pattern_ra1 = _black_stripes_thin1 | leftarm1 = FFFFFF | body1 = 000000 | rightarm1 = FFFFFF | shorts1 = 000000 | socks1 = FFFFFF | pattern_la2 = | pattern_b2 = _nikepark7to | pattern_ra2 = | leftarm2 = FF4200 | body2 = FF4200 | rightarm2 = FF4200 | shorts2 = 000000 | socks2 = 000000 }} '''Knattspyrnufélag Reykjavíkur''' ({{IPA|is|ˈkʰnahtˌspɪ(r)tnʏˌfjɛːˌlaːɣ ˈreiːcaˌviːkʏr̥}}, {{lit|Reykjavík Football Club}}), commonly abbreviated to '''KR''', is an Icelandic [[Association football|football]] club based in the [[Vesturbær]] district of the capital, [[Reykjavík]]. KR is the oldest{{cite web|url=https://www.mbl.is/greinasafn/grein/1498384/|title=Á þessum degi|website=Mbl.is|access-date=18 August 2020}} and most successful club in Icelandic football, having won the [[Besta deild karla]] championship 27 times, including the first season in 1912. It is also the most successful club in the [[Icelandic Men's Football Cup|Icelandic men's Cup]], with 14 titles including the first in 1960 and most recent in 2014. In 1964, KR was also the first Icelandic representative in the [[European Cup]]."}}
